answer.rationale: The competitor's price-cut attack on the SMB base creates immediate churn pressure, but memory_73 clearly demonstrates that promotional pricing acquired cohorts fail to survive renewal—exactly the opposite of your primary objective. Matching a discount would likely repeat that failure at scale. Instead, memory_44 shows enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows with superior pipeline quality, and memory_57 validates that referral incentives add qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention. A two-pronged approach is optimal: (1) Deploy enterprise_sales_assist to your account team to defend and upsell at-risk SMB accounts into higher-touch, higher-stickiness engagement paths—converting price sensitivity into relationship stickiness. (2) Run activation_messaging and simplified_onboarding for new SMB signups to improve completion and early product value, reducing price elasticity over time. The sales-assist lever addresses immediate churn among existing customers without a race-to-the-bottom discount; it preserves margin and cohort quality. A standard_experiment scope allows rapid learning while protecting downside—this is defensive but sustainable. Promotional pricing is rejected because the historical data is unambiguous: it trades long-term value for short-term acquisition vanity. Referral incentives could layer in later once you've stabilized retention.
